name: Lifeline Phone and Internet Discount
provider: Universal Service Administrative Company (Lifeline Support Center), for the FCC
description: Lifeline is a federal program that lowers the monthly cost of phone or internet service. If you qualify, you can get a monthly discount of up to $9.25 on phone, internet, or bundled service (up to $34.25 on qualifying Tribal lands). You qualify through your income or by taking part in programs such as SNAP or Medicaid. After you apply and are approved, you sign up with a participating phone or internet company.
contact: Lifeline Support Center: (800) 234-9473, 7 days a week 9:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m. ET; LifelineSupport@usac.org; mail: Lifeline Support Center, PO Box 1000, Horseheads, NY 14845

requirements.text: You qualify if you (or someone in your household) take part in Medicaid, SNAP, Supplemental Security Income (SSI), Federal Public Housing Assistance (including Section 8 vouchers and public housing), or the Veterans Pension and Survivors Benefit.

Or qualify by income: at 135% or less of the 2026 Federal Poverty Guidelines. Annual limits for the 48 contiguous states: 1 person $21,546; 2 $29,214; 3 $36,882; 4 $44,550; 5 $52,218; 6 $59,886; 7 $67,554; 8 $75,222; add $7,668 for each additional person.

Accepted proof includes a benefit award letter or benefits portal screenshot (program participation), a prior year's tax return or current annual income statement (income), and ID and address documents.

ways.title: Apply online
ways.detail: Apply on the Lifeline National Verifier to confirm you qualify, then choose a phone or internet company that offers Lifeline and sign up.

ways.title: Get help from the Lifeline Support Center
ways.detail: (800) 234-9473, 7 days a week, 9:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m. ET. They can also mail you an application.

ways.title: Apply by mail
ways.detail: Print an application (English or Spanish) and mail it to Lifeline Support Center, PO Box 1000, Horseheads, NY 14845.
